table.name: sale_record_events
columns: sale_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sales(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

identity.rule: kind is payload under the unique act identity and cannot create a second record for one act

checks: source_kind is one of sale_status, sale_customer, sale_settlement, sale_bulk_status, sale_bulk_update, return_create, return_edit, return_bulk
generation is an integer from 0 through 1000000
kind is one of the frozen F74 kinds
via is apply, undo, or redo
actor_username is null or at most 120 characters
subject is null or at most 240 characters
occurred_at is non-empty and at most 40 characters
changes_json is a valid JSON array with 1..12 elements and at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes
request_digest is null or a 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hex string
response_json is null or a valid JSON object no larger than 65536 UTF-8 bytes

rules: Reject unknown source_kind, kind, via, field, or field-for-kind combinations.
Require each change to contain exactly field, before, and after.
Require each side to be exactly known_value with value, known_none without value, or unknown without value.
Reject duplicate fields and equal before/after states.

Validate nested customer, membership, driver, item, item-list, payment, and payment-details shapes and scalar bounds. New customer values permit only stable id and display name; phone and address are forbidden. Existing undo receipts may retain their pre-existing private fields internally, but projection into changes_json removes them.

When response_json is used for direct-request idempotency, permit only the endpoint's fixed success/id/status/timestamp response keys. Never persist a request body, contact details, or arbitrary error payload in response_json.
Serialize only the validated normalized structure; never serialize request bodies or arbitrary audit variables.
server_validation_before_sql.batch_insert: One INSERT...SELECT FROM json_each(@events) statement writes all changed members. A 25-member bulk action or replay therefore adds exactly one D1 batch statement, not 25. Existing 500-statement and 512000-byte guards remain authoritative and run after the event statement is added.

writer_matrix.idempotency: Require a stable client_request_id for every non-noop status request. Save SHA-256 canonical request digest and response_json in the event. An exact retry returns response_json; reuse with another digest is 409. Event and sale/audit/stock writes share one guarded batch.
Require a stable client_request_id. Save canonical digest and response. Exact retry returns the saved response; conflicting reuse is 409. F72's active UI continues to use sale_bulk_update.

writer_matrix.writer: sale settlement/payment correction Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for each guarded replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor-scoped request receipt and generation guard are stable before the batch. Append event in the same batch as receipt creation or generation increment.

writer_matrix.writer: sale bulk status Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor/request receipt and generation guard. One validated json_each event insert covers up to 25 changed sale members atomically.

writer_matrix.writer: sale bulk customer/payment/driver Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor/request receipt and generation guard. One validated json_each event insert covers up to 25 changed sale members atomically.

The return's required client_request_id resolves to one durable returns.id before retry. Append the sale-status event in the same guarded batch as the status update; an existing return retry creates no second event. Supplier returns emit no sale event.

Require a stable client_request_id and expected_updated_at for edits. Save canonical digest and response. The event, return edit outcome, and resulting sale status must commit as one revision-guarded unit. Supplier returns emit no sale event.

writer_matrix.writer: return bulk status Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor/request receipt and generation guard. Compute one before/after sale status per distinct affected sale after the return statements and insert all events with one validated json_each statement. Supplier returns and non-status bulk fields emit no sale event.

legacy_cutover.detail: Load durable events first. Every post-cutover writer stamps its existing audit/action-history twin with the same source_kind, source_id, generation, and sale_id; existing receipt rows already expose that identity. Suppress a legacy candidate only when both it and an event expose an exact four-key match. Keep every old row with no exact tuple, including unknown legacy_sale_change.
legacy_cutover.count: Count sale_record_events directly. Each legacy receipt family contributes max(0, 1 + generation - exact matching event count for that source_kind/source_id/sale_id and generation range). Audit/return candidates use NOT EXISTS on the same four-key identity. No actor, state, status, or timestamp proximity matching.
legacy_cutover.parity: The detail and count paths share the same source-kind mapping and four-key anti-join test in focused SQLite fixtures.

immutability_and_lifecycle.trigger: BEFORE UPDATE always aborts. BEFORE DELETE aborts unless either the existing system_flags key maintenance has JSON mode restore, or the dedicated system_flags key sale_record_events_reset_guard has JSON mode reset and a non-empty token. Restore only needs DELETE plus INSERT, so it never weakens the UPDATE guard.
immutability_and_lifecycle.reset_sequence: Each reset uses one D1 batch whose first statement inserts sale_record_events_reset_guard with mode reset and a fresh non-empty token, whose next applicable statement deletes sale_record_events before sales, whose existing statements preserve child-first order, and whose last statement token-guards deletion of sale_record_events_reset_guard. A failed D1 batch rolls back the guard and every delete. The ordinary maintenance parser remains restore-only; the reset guard is internal and cannot outlive or expose a partially completed atomic batch.
backup: Add after sales and existing receipt parents in BACKUP_TABLES so restore inserts parents before events.
Add to SALE_REPLAY_RESTORE_BUNDLE so scoped restore cannot split events from sales/receipts.
The existing maintenance mode restore bypass permits reverse-order child deletion; event UPDATE remains forbidden.
immutability_and_lifecycle.factory_reset: Add sale_record_events before sales in FACTORY_RESET_TABLES and wrap that existing atomic batch with the dedicated reset guard statements.
immutability_and_lifecycle.reset_data: Add sale_record_events before sales in products+includeSales, sales, and all lists; wrap each existing atomic delete batch with the dedicated reset guard statements. The same ordered table list drives the pre-reset scoped backup and delete.
immutability_and_lifecycle.retention: No ephemeral-retention path references sale_record_events. Ordinary 21-day audit and action-history pruning cannot erase it.

permissions_and_audit.permissions: No new mutation route. Each append runs only inside its existing authorized writer/replay path after that path's permission check.
permissions_and_audit.audit: Existing audit logs remain. Record events add immutable display provenance and do not replace security/audit logging.

frontend_prerequisites: The ordinary sale-status caller must create one client_request_id when the user begins an action, persist it through unknown responses, and replace it only after a terminal success or a deliberate new action.
The legacy direct-customer caller, if retained, and customer-return edit caller must follow the same stable client_request_id lifecycle. Return edit must continue sending expected_updated_at.
Do not enable a backend requirement until these callers and focused unknown-response retry tests are integrated in the same release candidate.
required_tests: Native SQLite Apply/Undo/Redo for settlement, sale bulk status, sale bulk update, and return bulk status.
Native SQLite create/edit customer return sale-status before/after and supplier non-event.
Stable retry returns prior response; conflicting request-id reuse fails; concurrent revision loses atomically.
Maximum 25-member bulk fixtures prove exactly one added statement and remain below existing 500/512000 bounds.
Malformed kind/field/state/nested value, 13 changes, oversized JSON, duplicate field, and equal-state events fail before SQL.
Migration CHECKs, append-only triggers, reset maintenance order, backup/restore dependency coverage, factory reset, sales reset, all reset, products includeSales.
Audit pruning leaves every new event and exact legacy fallback; count equals detail for mixed pre/post migration history.
